title: The Audit
logline: Michael stages a fake functional office for a surprise corporate auditor, while Andy's arrival sparks Dwight's secret war, Jim and Pam's Jell-O prank lands on the potluck table, and the beets give away Angela and Dwight's secret.
outline: A: Michael stages a "functional office" for surprise auditor Gerald Boyd, who only wants receipts; the folding chair for Toby becomes the one honest thing. B: Andy's welcome song sparks Dwight's secret war; Jim and Pam's Jell-O prank escalates onto the potluck table in the audit; Dwight and Andy reach an armed truce. C: Dwight's labeled beets and Angela's public thanks; Oscar and Kevin know, nobody says it. Order: cold_open, A, B, C, A, B, A, C, B, A, B, tag.
theme: Everyone performs for someone, and the real thing is what happens when the performance slips.
storySoFar: Michael is still chasing Jan's approval after the Idol flop and the Dundies toast that died in silence; Jan keeps sending maybes. Jim and Pam keep pranking Dwight, and their latest Jell-O escalation has now reached Angela's potluck. Jim noticed Pam's earrings; Roy noticed two hours late and got it wrong. Roy keeps postponing the wedding. Angela and Dwight's secret is an open office joke nobody says aloud; Kevin still says "Nobody say nothing." Andy Bernard has arrived from Stamford, sang a welcome, and Dwight has declared a secret war. Corporate auditor Gerald Boyd has been announced for Thursday. Michael keeps setting out a folding chair for Toby, who is still not invited. Stanley is at 212 days.

stateChanges.arc: Will They, Won't They: Jim and Pam
stateChanges.progress: Jim's Jell-O prank hits Angela's potluck during the audit; Pam calls out the escalation. Earrings callback in tag: Pam says Roy didn't notice again, Jim says they're the good ones.
Gerald Boyd passes the office by a hair ('barely') and sits in the folding chair meant for Toby, who finally sits in it. Michael tears up behind a receipt and hides it.
Andy's welcome sparked Dwight's secret war, then an armed truce: Dwight keeps the title (61/39), Andy keeps the crowd.
Angela thanks Dwight publicly for checking the fax; Oscar and Kevin know; nobody says anything.

stateChanges.text: Dwight's lime Jell-O trophy, 'Dwight Schrute, Quality Dessert', wobbles on the shelf as a laugh button.
Gerald Boyd has audited 41 branches; Scranton is the first to set out a chair for nobody. Gerald gave Scranton a 'barely' pass. Possible return for a later audit.
Michael's folding chair for Toby is now officially sat in by Toby once.

scenes.recap: Andy Bernard arrives from Stamford and bursts into an a cappella welcome.

beats.text: Everyone look busy. Andy Bernard is coming from Stamford, and he is a Cornell man.
Is he cute? Because Ryan is a nine, and I'm not saying it's a competition.

beats.caption: bursts into an a cappella welcome, arms wide

beats.text: Scranton! Stamford sends its love and its best tenor!
Question: What is that tie? Answer: Better than mine. I'll allow it. For now.

lines: Andy Bernard has a better tie, a worse voice, and a Cornell sweatshirt. I am going to fix one of those.

beats.text: Big Tuna! Jim Halpert, my Big Tuna!
Hey, Andy.
That's what she said.

beats.caption: Nobody reacts.

scenes.recap: Michael announces a surprise corporate audit and demands a functional office.

beats.text: Corporate is sending a man. Gerald Boyd. Corporate Auditor. Surprise audit, Thursday, nine a.m.
Two hundred and fourteen days. I am not available for surprises.
We are going to be a functional office. A functional office. Nobody say the word Jell-O.
Question: Is Jell-O functional? Answer: False.
Actually, a surprise audit means he has already seen the receipts.
Oscar, I don't want to hear one 'actually' until Thursday.
I could do the HR binder. For the audit. Just in case.
Toby, you're not invited to the audit.

lines: Gerald Boyd has never smiled. Not once. I will be the first person to make him smile. Or at least sign something.

beats.text: I've been audited in three countries. One of them was a boat.

beats.caption: Nobody moves. Somewhere, a stapler clicks.

scenes.recap: Jim and Pam plan a bigger Jell-O prank while Andy begs to be let in and Dwight declares secret war.

beats.text: Dwight got his stapler back out of the Jell-O, so now he thinks he won.
Jim, we said one prank a week.
This is one prank. It's just a bigger bowl.
Big Tuna, I'm in. I was in every Cornell prank. Including the one with the tuba.
No, Andy.
Okay.

beats.caption: tapes a lime Jell-O cup under Dwight's keyboard tray

beats.text: Question: Why are you two whispering by my desk? False. You are not whispering. You are plotting.
It's a surprise party. For you.
I do not have birthday parties. I have Schrute Farms.

lines: Pam wants a small prank. I am picking a small prank. The small prank is Dwight's entire keyboard.
Andy Bernard has been here forty minutes and already wants in on my pranks. I declare war. It is a secret war. He does not know. Do not tell him.

scenes.recap: Dwight's beets are labeled DO NOT TOUCH with Angela's name, and the break room pretends not to notice.

beats.caption: eats a beet from a Tupperware labeled DO NOT TOUCH, ANGELA'S

beats.text: Dwight, did you label these beets?
They are from Schrute Farms. They are not for communal use. Question: Would you like one? Answer: Yes.
Actually, the label says DO NOT TOUCH, and then your name. That is a very specific sentence.
Oscar. Your opinion has been noted and filed.
Nobody say nothing.

beats.caption: Nobody says anything. Kevin chews.

lines: Dwight checks things for me. I ask him to. I thank him, in public, which is normal. Nothing is happening in this break room. Nothing has ever happened in this break room.

beats.caption: pours a glass of water very slowly, with great dignity

scenes.recap: Michael rehearses a functional office with the staff, playing Gerald Boyd himself.

beats.text: Places. This is a normal Wednesday. Stanley, you love your job.
Did I stutter? I don't love my job. I love two hundred and fourteen days.

beats.caption: types with one finger, very seriously, at a blank screen

beats.text: Perfect. Now I am Gerald Boyd. I am monotone. I am here for a receipt.
Chili. Receipt.
Kevin, that is a napkin.
I was an auditor once. In Ohio. Briefly.
Michael, audits don't work like this. They're quiet. Mostly they're just quiet.
Toby, quiet is not a personality.

lines: Gerald Boyd will walk in and see a functional office. I will not say Thursday. I will not cry. I may cry at a receipt.

beats.caption: Everyone sits perfectly still. It is the least functional…

scenes.recap: Dwight hands Andy a rulebook and Andy starts singing; Michael picks Andy as his new singalong buddy.

beats.text: Question: Do you know the rules? Answer: No. I wrote them. Twelve.
Number seven says no singing. Dwight, that's adorable.
Number seven is for you.

beats.caption: hums the Here Comes Treble intro, very quietly, at Dwight

beats.text: False. I will not be serenaded at my desk.
Andy! Sing the one from the car. Sing it for Dwight. And for me.

beats.caption: belts out a verse with his whole chest, reaching for the high note
claps along, a half beat behind

beats.text: Michael, I am your right hand. Question: Is Andy your right hand? Answer: False.
You're my right hand, Dwight. Andy's a left hand. We have two hands!

lines: Andy Bernard is a threat. I have studied him. He is wearing a tie I would like to own. This is a secret war. I am telling you. I am not telling him.

scenes.recap: Gerald Boyd arrives early, demands receipts, and sits down in front of a folding chair with no name tag.

beats.text: Gerald Boyd, Corporate. It's eight fifty-two. I'm early.
Hi. Welcome to... we're functional!
Gerald! You're early! Welcome to the most functional—
I'd like to see your receipts, Mr. Scott.
Mr. Scott, is this a receipt for six shakers? For Dundies?
Those were mandatory. It was very successful.

lines: Nobody asked me about the folding chair. I'm not invited. But I'd like to sit in it once. Just once. For the record.

beats.caption: Gerald sighs. The sigh goes on for a while.

scenes.recap: Angela thanks Dwight in public for checking the fax, and Oscar almost says it.

beats.text: Dwight, thank you for checking the fax. Again. Your thoroughness is noted.
It is my job. Question: Is there a fax? Answer: No. There is a copier. I checked it anyway.
Nobody say nothing.
Kevin, I'm not saying anything. Actually—I'm not saying anything.

lines: Everyone in this building knows. They know because Angela said 'thorough' like it was a lyric. I am an adult. I am not saying it.

scenes.recap: Gerald starts the findings during Angela's potluck, and Jim's Jell-O stapler lands on the snack table.

beats.text: I'm going to go through the findings. Fourteen missing receipts. One folding chair.
Gerald, first, we have a snack. Angela's potluck. It's very functional.
The potluck is not a snack. It is a potluck.

beats.caption: sets a lime Jell-O stapler on the potluck table, where it was not supposed to go

beats.text: Jim, that's Angela's table.
The mold was for the desk. The desk is now a table.

beats.caption: pokes a cup of lime Jell-O, which jiggles
The Jell-O jiggles. Nobody laughs.

beats.text: Question: Who put Jell-O on the audit? Answer: Jim.
It's not the Jell-O's fault, Dwight.
Gerald, I can sing about the snack.
No.

scenes.recap: Gerald delivers a barely passing verdict and makes Toby sit in the folding chair.

beats.text: Mr. Scott, I've audited forty-one branches. Yours has fourteen missing receipts and a potluck on the table.
Forty-one. Gerald, were any of them the best?
No.
I just wanted you to see a functional office.
I saw a folding chair for someone who isn't invited.
Toby's not invited.
Mr. Flenderson. Sit down.
This is... actually comfortable.
It is the most comfortable folding chair I have ever sat in. I've sat in many.

lines: He said we passed. He said 'passed,' and then he said 'barely.' I'm going to frame the word barely. I'm not crying. It's the Jell-O.

beats.text: Two hundred and thirteen.

beats.caption: Michael tears up behind a receipt.

scenes.recap: Dwight and Andy agree to an armed truce over a single song, and Jim gets to witness it.

beats.text: Dwight. Truce?
Terms. Number one: No singing at the desk.
I'll sing at the copier.
Acceptable. Number two: You do not tell Michael I am fond of you.
You're fond of me?
False.

beats.caption: sings the first line of a truce song, very quietly, just for Dwight
joins on harmony, flat, without moving his face

beats.text: Michael will always choose me.
Sixty-forty. You.
Sixty-one, thirty-nine. I will not argue a decimal.
Big Tuna, witness this. We're allies.
I'm witnessing it. It's the least strange thing I've seen today.

lines: Andy Bernard keeps the crowd. I keep the title. Stamford has no beets. I will be watching him anyway.

scenes.recap: The next morning, Stanley counts down, Kevin repeats his line, and Dwight's Jell-O trophy wobbles.

beats.text: Two hundred and twelve.
Nobody say nothing.

beats.caption: dusts the lime Jell-O trophy labeled 'Dwight Schrute, Quality Dessert'

beats.text: Hey, Pam. The earrings.
Roy didn't notice. Again.
They're the good ones.

beats.caption: Pam smiles down at her desk.

beats.text: Question: Who keeps putting Jell-O on my Quality Dessert? Answer: Jim.

beats.caption: wobbles on the shelf, all by itself, and nobody touches it
